# IMO 2008 Problem 4 — Solution

**Problem.** Find all $f:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that
$$\frac{f(w)^2+f(x)^2}{f(y)^2+f(z)^2}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}\qquad\text{whenever }wx=yz.$$

**Answer.** $\;f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2}\;$ for constants $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$ with $\alpha+\beta>0$.

---

## Reduction to a functional equation for $g=f^2$

Set $g(t)=f(t)^2>0$. The condition reads
$$\frac{g(w)+g(x)}{g(y)+g(z)}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}\qquad(wx=yz).$$

Fix $P>0$. For any two pairs $(w,x),(y,z)$ with $wx=yz=P$, cross‑multiplying gives
$$\frac{g(w)+g(x)}{w^2+x^2}=\frac{g(y)+g(z)}{y^2+z^2}.$$
So this ratio depends only on the product $P=wx$; call it $h(P)$. Hence
$$g(w)+g(x)=h(wx)(w^2+x^2)\qquad\forall\,w,x>0.\tag{1}$$

Set $x=1$ and let $A=g(1)>0$: $g(w)+A=h(w)(w^2+1)$, so $h(w)=\dfrac{g(w)+A}{w^2+1}$. Substituting back into (1),
$$(g(w)+g(x))\bigl((wx)^2+1\bigr)=(g(wx)+A)(w^2+x^2).\tag{E}$$

## Isolating the "additive" part

Define $\varphi(t)=g(t)-At^2$. Taking $x=1/w$ in (E) (so $wx=1$):
$$g(w)+g(1/w)=A\!\left(w^2+\tfrac1{w^2}\right),$$
i.e. $\varphi(w)+\varphi(1/w)=0$ (antisymmetry; in particular $\varphi(1)=0$). Substituting $g=At^2+\varphi$ into (E), the $A$‑terms cancel and leave
$$(\varphi(w)+\varphi(x))(w^2x^2+1)=\varphi(wx)(w^2+x^2).\tag{$\Phi$}$$

## Logarithmic form

Write $w=e^a,\ x=e^b,\ \psi(a)=\varphi(e^a)$. Then $\psi$ is odd ($\psi(-a)=-\psi(a)$, $\psi(0)=0$), and using
$$w^2x^2+1=2e^{a+b}\cosh(a+b),\qquad w^2+x^2=2e^{a+b}\cosh(a-b),$$
equation $(\Phi)$ becomes
$$(\psi(a)+\psi(b))\cosh(a+b)=\psi(a+b)\cosh(a-b).\tag{$\Psi$}$$

For $a\ne 0$ set $\psi(a)=\sinh(2a)\,\chi(a)$. Since $\psi$ is odd and $\sinh(2a)$ is odd, $\chi$ is **even**. Using
$$\sinh 2a+\sinh 2b=2\sinh(a+b)\cosh(a-b),\quad \sinh(2(a+b))=2\sinh(a+b)\cosh(a+b),$$
equation $(\Psi)$ reduces (divide by $\cosh(a+b)$) to
$$\sinh(2a)\,\chi(a)+\sinh(2b)\,\chi(b)=(\sinh 2a+\sinh 2b)\,\chi(a+b).\tag{$\star$}$$

## $\chi$ is constant

Take any $s,t>0$ and put $S=\sinh 2s,\ T=\sinh 2t,\ U=\sinh(2(s+t))$.

* From $(\star)$ with $(a,b)=(s,t)$: $\;\chi(s+t)=\dfrac{S\,\chi(s)+T\,\chi(t)}{S+T}.$
* From $(\star)$ with $(a,b)=(s+t,-t)$ (using $\chi(-t)=\chi(t)$ and $\sinh(-2t)=-T$): $\;\chi(s)=\dfrac{U\,\chi(s+t)-T\,\chi(t)}{U-T}.$

Substituting the first into the second and simplifying:
$$\chi(s)\cdot T\,(U-S-T)=T\,(U-S-T)\,\chi(t).$$

Now $T=\sinh 2t>0$, and
$$U-S-T=\sinh 2s(\cosh 2t-1)+\sinh 2t(\cosh 2s-1)>0\qquad(s,t>0),$$
since every factor is positive. Therefore $\chi(s)=\chi(t)$ for all $s,t>0$. By evenness $\chi$ is constant on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$; call the constant $c$.

## Determining $g$ and $f$

Thus $\psi(a)=c\sinh(2a)$, i.e.
$$\varphi(t)=c\sinh(2\ln t)=\tfrac{c}{2}(t^2-t^{-2}).$$
Renaming the constant, $\varphi(t)=c\,(t^2-t^{-2})$, and
$$g(t)=At^2+c(t^2-t^{-2})=(A+c)t^2-c\,t^{-2}.$$
Set $\alpha=A+c$ and $\beta=-c$; then $\alpha+\beta=A=g(1)>0$ and
$$g(t)=\alpha t^2+\frac{\beta}{t^2}.$$

**Positivity forces $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$:** if $\alpha<0$ then $g(t)\to-\infty$ as $t\to\infty$; if $\beta<0$ then $g(t)\to-\infty$ as $t\to0^+$. Conversely, $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ with $\alpha+\beta>0$ gives $g(t)>0$ for every $t>0$. So
$$f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0,\ \alpha+\beta>0.$$

## Verification

For $f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2}$,
$$f(w)^2+f(x)^2=\alpha(w^2+x^2)+\beta\!\left(\tfrac1{w^2}+\tfrac1{x^2}\right)=(w^2+x^2)\!\left(\alpha+\frac{\beta}{(wx)^2}\right),$$
and similarly $f(y)^2+f(z)^2=(y^2+z^2)\bigl(\alpha+\beta/(yz)^2\bigr)$. Since $wx=yz$,
$$\frac{f(w)^2+f(x)^2}{f(y)^2+f(z)^2}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}.\quad\checkmark$$

---

**Conclusion.** The solutions are exactly
$$\boxed{\,f(x)=\sqrt{\alpha x^2+\dfrac{\beta}{x^2}}\;,\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge 0,\ \alpha+\beta>0\,}$$
(including the two pure families $f(x)=\sqrt{\alpha}\,x$ when $\beta=0$ and $f(x)=\sqrt{\beta}/x$ when $\alpha=0$).

# IMO 2008 Problem 4 — Solution

**Problem.** Find all $f:\mathbb{R}_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that
$$\frac{f(w)^2+f(x)^2}{f(y)^2+f(z)^2}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}\qquad\text{whenever }wx=yz.$$

**Answer.** $\;f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2}\;$ for constants $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$ with $\alpha+\beta>0$.

---

## Reduction to a functional equation for $g=f^2$

Set $g(t)=f(t)^2>0$. The condition reads
$$\frac{g(w)+g(x)}{g(y)+g(z)}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}\qquad(wx=yz).$$

Fix $P>0$. For any two pairs $(w,x),(y,z)$ with $wx=yz=P$, cross‑multiplying gives
$$\frac{g(w)+g(x)}{w^2+x^2}=\frac{g(y)+g(z)}{y^2+z^2}.$$
So this ratio depends only on the product $P=wx$; call it $h(P)$. Hence
$$g(w)+g(x)=h(wx)(w^2+x^2)\qquad\forall\,w,x>0.\tag{1}$$

Set $x=1$ and let $A=g(1)>0$: $g(w)+A=h(w)(w^2+1)$, so $h(w)=\dfrac{g(w)+A}{w^2+1}$. Substituting back into (1),
$$(g(w)+g(x))\bigl((wx)^2+1\bigr)=(g(wx)+A)(w^2+x^2).\tag{E}$$

## Isolating the "additive" part

Define $\varphi(t)=g(t)-At^2$. Taking $x=1/w$ in (E) (so $wx=1$):
$$g(w)+g(1/w)=A\!\left(w^2+\tfrac1{w^2}\right),$$
i.e. $\varphi(w)+\varphi(1/w)=0$ (antisymmetry; in particular $\varphi(1)=0$). Substituting $g=At^2+\varphi$ into (E), the $A$‑terms cancel and leave
$$(\varphi(w)+\varphi(x))(w^2x^2+1)=\varphi(wx)(w^2+x^2).\tag{$\Phi$}$$

## Logarithmic form

Write $w=e^a,\ x=e^b,\ \psi(a)=\varphi(e^a)$. Then $\psi$ is odd ($\psi(-a)=-\psi(a)$, $\psi(0)=0$), and using
$$w^2x^2+1=2e^{a+b}\cosh(a+b),\qquad w^2+x^2=2e^{a+b}\cosh(a-b),$$
equation $(\Phi)$ becomes
$$(\psi(a)+\psi(b))\cosh(a+b)=\psi(a+b)\cosh(a-b).\tag{$\Psi$}$$

For $a\ne 0$ set $\psi(a)=\sinh(2a)\,\chi(a)$. Since $\psi$ is odd and $\sinh(2a)$ is odd, $\chi$ is **even**. Using
$$\sinh 2a+\sinh 2b=2\sinh(a+b)\cosh(a-b),\quad \sinh(2(a+b))=2\sinh(a+b)\cosh(a+b),$$
equation $(\Psi)$ reduces (divide by $\cosh(a+b)$) to
$$\sinh(2a)\,\chi(a)+\sinh(2b)\,\chi(b)=(\sinh 2a+\sinh 2b)\,\chi(a+b).\tag{$\star$}$$

## $\chi$ is constant

Take any $s,t>0$ and put $S=\sinh 2s,\ T=\sinh 2t,\ U=\sinh(2(s+t))$.

* From $(\star)$ with $(a,b)=(s,t)$: $\;\chi(s+t)=\dfrac{S\,\chi(s)+T\,\chi(t)}{S+T}.$
* From $(\star)$ with $(a,b)=(s+t,-t)$ (using $\chi(-t)=\chi(t)$ and $\sinh(-2t)=-T$): $\;\chi(s)=\dfrac{U\,\chi(s+t)-T\,\chi(t)}{U-T}.$

Substituting the first into the second and simplifying:
$$\chi(s)\cdot T\,(U-S-T)=T\,(U-S-T)\,\chi(t).$$

Now $T=\sinh 2t>0$, and
$$U-S-T=\sinh 2s(\cosh 2t-1)+\sinh 2t(\cosh 2s-1)>0\qquad(s,t>0),$$
since every factor is positive. Therefore $\chi(s)=\chi(t)$ for all $s,t>0$. By evenness $\chi$ is constant on $\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$; call the constant $c$.

## Determining $g$ and $f$

Thus $\psi(a)=c\sinh(2a)$, i.e.
$$\varphi(t)=c\sinh(2\ln t)=\tfrac{c}{2}(t^2-t^{-2}).$$
Renaming the constant, $\varphi(t)=c\,(t^2-t^{-2})$, and
$$g(t)=At^2+c(t^2-t^{-2})=(A+c)t^2-c\,t^{-2}.$$
Set $\alpha=A+c$ and $\beta=-c$; then $\alpha+\beta=A=g(1)>0$ and
$$g(t)=\alpha t^2+\frac{\beta}{t^2}.$$

**Positivity forces $\alpha,\beta\ge 0$:** if $\alpha<0$ then $g(t)\to-\infty$ as $t\to\infty$; if $\beta<0$ then $g(t)\to-\infty$ as $t\to0^+$. Conversely, $\alpha,\beta\ge0$ with $\alpha+\beta>0$ gives $g(t)>0$ for every $t>0$. So
$$f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2},\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge0,\ \alpha+\beta>0.$$

## Verification

For $f(t)=\sqrt{\alpha t^2+\beta/t^2}$,
$$f(w)^2+f(x)^2=\alpha(w^2+x^2)+\beta\!\left(\tfrac1{w^2}+\tfrac1{x^2}\right)=(w^2+x^2)\!\left(\alpha+\frac{\beta}{(wx)^2}\right),$$
and similarly $f(y)^2+f(z)^2=(y^2+z^2)\bigl(\alpha+\beta/(yz)^2\bigr)$. Since $wx=yz$,
$$\frac{f(w)^2+f(x)^2}{f(y)^2+f(z)^2}=\frac{w^2+x^2}{y^2+z^2}.\quad\checkmark$$

---

**Conclusion.** The solutions are exactly
$$\boxed{\,f(x)=\sqrt{\alpha x^2+\dfrac{\beta}{x^2}}\;,\qquad \alpha,\beta\ge 0,\ \alpha+\beta>0\,}$$
(including the two pure families $f(x)=\sqrt{\alpha}\,x$ when $\beta=0$ and $f(x)=\sqrt{\beta}/x$ when $\alpha=0$).
